subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner has or can form two linear equations in two unknowns
use when elimination/substitution execution is unstable
anchor: A system asks for values satisfying both equations at once; elimination creates an equivalent simpler system by combining whole equations legally.
ordinary_language_bridge: Treat each equation as a complete statement. Scale or combine whole equations so one variable cancels, then verify the pair in both originals.
reconstruction_route: if needed scale an entire equation

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: same pair of equations and same elimination target
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: subtract whole equations versus cancelling unlike/unmatched terms
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which combination preserves a system with the same solution?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: whole-equation operations and aligned like terms

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: individual terms may be cancelled across equations without applying an operation to the whole equations
misconception_discriminator.probe: present two elimination lines and require the whole-equation operation to be named
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner identifies scaling/addition/subtraction of complete equations

repair_route: perform one system operation per line
verification_method: substitute the ordered pair into both original equations
known_limitations: does not decide when substitution is more efficient
